newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo forex spot trading volume hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo forex spot trading volume hits record high.

text.p: The volume of dollar/yen spot transactions on the Tokyo foreign exchange market hit a record high in fiscal 1996, and overall spot and swap transaction volume was at a six-year high, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Tuesday.
It said the volume of spot dollar/yen transactions through brokers rose to a record $2.59 trillion.
The overall volume of dollar/yen swap and spot transactions through brokers rose to nearly $5.91 trillion in the year to March 31, second only to about $5.96 trillion in fiscal 1990/91.

"I think the volume rose on aggressive movements by institutional investors in currency markets, such as life insurers, in connection with their overseas investments," said Junichi Kodama of Chase Manhattan Bank in Tokyo.

In the year to January, Japanese life insurers boosted their foreign bond holdings by 28.3 percent to 16.99 trillion yen, although from February to April the capital flow appears for various reasons to have slowed to a trickle.
Kodama said the planned deregulation of Japan's financial markets will continue to increase the volume of foreign exchange trading as it will attract more investors to Tokyo markets.

A senior dealer at a Japanese bank said a rise in trading volume was mostly due to a recent boom in foreign bond investments, such as dual-currency bonds, by retail investors. This trend led securities houses to actively trade in currency markets in order to keep feeding such yield-hungry individual investors, he added.
"Individual investors used to look for investment opportunities domestically, but now they are eager to invest in foreign bonds," he said.
A record 2.4 trillion yen worth of dual-currency bonds was issued in 1996, underwriting sources said.

The bank dealer said financial institutions could take larger positions after rules limiting the daily volume of their foreign currency exposure were eased in April 1996, which also helped push overall trading volume higher.
